note: Product-convergence matrix: core payments companies (config.UNIVERSE 'core') by nine product lines, each cell with status (live, beta, announced, discontinued, none), launch date where the source states one, and the company page or release it comes from. Afterpay and PayPal Pay Later are recorded under their parents (Block/Square, PayPal). Undated product pages give status as of last_checked only; launch_date is null where no page read stated it. Pairs not listed are not covered, not confirmed absent.

rows.caveat: Stripe's core product: online card and alternative-method acceptance (the page cites 125+ payment methods). Undated product page; status is as of the date read. Launch date not stated on the page.
rows.curator_notes: Page heading 'Unified, global payments to grow your revenue'; 'Accept payments online, in person, and around the world'.

rows.source_name: Stripe newsroom: Stripe announces Stripe Terminal
rows.caveat: Stripe Terminal, a developer-programmable in-person acceptance product announced in the US in September 2018. Stripe sells readers and SDKs; it is not a full restaurant or retail POS suite. The current product page lists acceptance across 39 markets.
rows.curator_notes: 'SAN FRANCISCO — Stripe today unveiled Stripe Terminal, a new product that extends Stripe's infrastructure to the physical world', dated September 17, 2018; stripe.com/terminal says 'across 39 markets'.

rows.source_name: Stripe newsroom: Stripe launches Stripe Issuing
rows.caveat: Stripe Issuing, an API for businesses to create their own physical and virtual cards; available in the US at launch, by invite. Later geographic expansion is not reflected in this date.
rows.curator_notes: 'Today Stripe unveiled Stripe Issuing, a new product that allows online businesses and platforms to create their own credit and debit cards'; 'available to businesses in the United States today. To request an invite'.

rows.source_name: Stripe blog: Our top product updates from Stripe Tour New York
rows.caveat: Stablecoin (USDC) payment acceptance in Stripe checkout, announced as available on 2024-10-09; trade coverage at the time described it as open to US businesses, settling in USD. Stripe later closed its Bridge acquisition on 2025-02-04 and announced stablecoin balances in Stripe Treasury in May 2025 with waitlist access. Current status is live.
rows.curator_notes: stripe.com/blog/our-top-product-updates-from-stripe-tour-ny, 'October 9, 2024', Will Gaybrick, under 'Optimized Checkout Suite': 'You can now accept stablecoin payments from customers around the world.' US-only scope from trade press (PYMNTS/The Block 2024-10-10), not from the Stripe page. Bridge close: stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-completes-bridge-acquisition, February 4, 2025. Treasury stablecoins blog 2025-05-20 'You can join the waitlist'.

rows.caveat: Stripe Treasury business accounts for Stripe users (the page says 'Open a bank account in minutes'), held through partner banks. Undated product page; launch date not stated on the page. The platform (embedded) version of Treasury predates this direct offer.
rows.curator_notes: 'Business banking and payments, together on Stripe'; 'Open a bank account 1 in minutes with no minimums or monthly fees.'

rows.caveat: Multicurrency balances (USD, EUR, GBP shown) and payouts to 160+ countries inside Stripe Treasury. Undated product page; launch date not stated. Scope and currency list vary by country.
rows.curator_notes: 'Send one-time or recurring payouts to 160+ countries in minutes, and reduce FX costs by paying out in local currencies or stablecoins'; account mock shows USD/GBP/EUR balances.

rows.caveat: Stripe Card, a Mastercard spend card drawn on the Treasury balance with 2% cashback; a debit-style business card, not a charge card with a credit line. Undated product page.
rows.curator_notes: 'Earn 2% cashback on purchases wherever Mastercard is accepted—available for both physical and virtual Stri[pe cards]'.

rows.caveat: Stripe does not lend to shoppers itself; it offers third-party buy now, pay later methods (for example Klarna, Affirm) at checkout. Absence of an own-balance-sheet BNPL product is as of the date read.
rows.curator_notes: 'Access 125+ payment methods—from buy now, pay later options that can boost eligible revenue by up to 14%'; no Stripe-branded consumer lending product on page.
